newsitem.title: USA: Time running short for tobacco deal--US Sen Lott.
newsitem.headline: Time running short for tobacco deal--US Sen Lott.

text.p: Senate Majority Leader Trent Lott said on Wednesday that time may be running short for a negotiated settlement between the tobacco industry and the states suing it.

"Time is beginning to work against them. The calender is working against them," the Mississippi Republican told reporters. "The legislative calender gets to be a problem," he said. "With every passing week, with every passing month, our schedule fills up." A negotiated settlement is likely to require some type of action by Congress.

Lott declined to speculate on the status of the negotiations between the tobacco companies and the 32 state attorneys general who have filed lawsuits in a bid to recoup the health care costs of smokers.
But Lott said that, in general, the longer negotiations take and the more people get involved, "the more people want a piece of the action," the harder it is to reach an agreement.

Negotiations are set to resume next week. The timing is crucial as the date approaches for the first trial of a state's lawsuit against the industry to recoup Medicaid costs for smoking-related illnesses.
On Tuesday, House Speaker Newt Gingrich said there was only a one-in-three chance that a broad settlement of tobacco-related lawsuits would be reached and then be approved by Congress.
